lines.text: Some three hundred islands in the western Pacific, ruled in turn by four foreign powers, then free. This is the story of Palau.
Palauans lived on these islands for some three thousand years. Haruo Remeliik, born in 1933, would become the first president.
In 1944 American forces landed on Peleliu, then held by Japan. It became one of the hardest battles of the Pacific war.
After the war, from 1947, the United States ran Palau as part of a United Nations trust territory.
Surangel Whipps Junior, born in 1968, would one day be elected president, in 2021.
In the eighties Palau worked out a compact of free association with the United States, and its first president, Remeliik, was killed in 1985.
In 1994 Palau became independent, in free association with the United States.
In 2006 the government moved to a new capital, Ngerulmud, on the largest island.
In 2012 the mushroom-shaped Rock Islands of the southern lagoon were listed as a World Heritage Site.
And in 2015 Palau set aside most of its waters as a national marine sanctuary, one of the largest in the world.
From ancient voyagers to guardians of the ocean, Palau's small islands tell a large story.
